children: Hudbay Minerals notched record quarterly revenue on the back of increased copper and gold production and higher metals prices.

The Canadian miner's net earnings attributable to owners came in at $149.5 million, or 34 cents a share, for the third quarter. That was down from $222.4 million, or 56 cents a share, a year earlier but up on the previous quarter's $137.4 million, or 34 cents a share.
On an adjusted basis, per-share earnings also came in at 34 cents, in line with the mean forecast of analysts polled by FactSet.
Revenue for the three months more than doubled to $765.9 million, versus $346.8 million in the same period last year and the roughly $730 million anticipated by analysts.

Hudbay, which operates in Peru and Canada and is building mines in the U.S., produced 30,152 metric tons of copper in the latest quarter, up from 28,267 tons the quarter before and 24,205 tons last year. Gold output increased 36% quarter over quarter and 30% from a year earlier to 69,513 troy ounces.

Chief Executive Peter Kukielski said Hudbay is on track to deliver a 12th consecutive year of meeting annual copper production guidance and the sixth straight year of achieving its annual gold target.
Hudbay continues to expect production to reach 110,000 to 138,000 tons of copper this year, and 217,000 to 272,000 ounces of gold.

The miner has faced higher diesel prices this year, but said cost control overall has been resilient. For the full year, it now expects sustaining cash costs in a range of $1.40 to $1.80 a pound of copper against an earlier estimate of $1.70 to $2.10 per pound.

Hudbay said its Peru operations showed steady operating performance in the third quarter with production of 20,572 tons of copper and 5,267 ounces of gold. The Manitoba operations produced 57,261 ounces of gold, 3,012 tons of copper, 3,691 tons of zinc and 268,346 ounces of silver in the quarter.

Hudbay and partner Mitsubishi last month formally approved construction of the Copper World project in Arizona, which promises to be the next major copper mine in the U.S. with projected annual copper production of 102,000 metric tons over the first 10 years of mining. The development is expected to boost Hudbay's copper output each year to about 250,000 tons, with first output set for the second half of 2029.

It comes after the Toronto-based company in June closed a roughly $1.48 billion deal to buy the outstanding shares of Arizona Sonoran, growing its footprint in southern Arizona. The combination put Hudbay on a path to grow annual copper production to more than 350,000 tons with the staged development of its Cactus project in the state.
